# React store scoping and lifecycle

Use React context to choose a store instance for a subtree, then `useClassyStore` to subscribe to that instance. This is useful for independent forms, editors, nested workspaces, and request-scoped server rendering.

The runnable [scoped editors demo](https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/demos/#/scoped-stores) shows two independent editors and a nested editor. Its [source](https://github.com/codeBelt/classy-store/tree/main/examples/react/src/demos/scoped-store) is an application example built from existing APIs; there is no new context factory to install.

## Define a typed context

Share the context definition across the application. Create store instances inside each provider, so server requests and sibling providers cannot accidentally share mutable state.

```ts
// editorStore.ts
export type EditorData = {title: string; body: string};

export class EditorStore {
  title: string;
  body: string;

  constructor(initialData: EditorData) {
    this.title = initialData.title;
    this.body = initialData.body;
  }

  setTitle(title: string) { this.title = title; }
  setBody(body: string) { this.body = body; }
}
```

```ts
// editorStoreContext.ts
import {createContext} from 'react';
import type {EditorStore} from './editorStore';

export const EditorStoreContext = createContext<EditorStore | null>(null);
```

```ts
// hooks/useEditorStore.ts
import {useContext} from 'react';
import {EditorStoreContext} from '../editorStoreContext';

export function useEditorStore() {
  const store = useContext(EditorStoreContext);
  if (!store) {
    throw new Error('useEditorStore must be used within EditorStoreProvider');
  }
  return store;
}
```

The hook returns a typed mutable `EditorStore`, with its methods intact. It fails clearly when a provider is missing. React resolves the [closest matching provider](https://react.dev/reference/react/useContext), so a nested provider overrides the instance only for its own subtree.

## Let the provider own creation and effects

The example provider initializes once per mount and captures the initial hydration data before starting persistence:

```tsx
// components/editorStoreProvider/EditorStoreProvider.tsx
import {useLocalStore} from '@codebelt/classy-store/react';
import {prepareStoreForHydration} from '@codebelt/classy-store/react/server';
import {persist, type StorageAdapter} from '@codebelt/classy-store/utils';
import {type ReactNode, useEffect} from 'react';
import {type EditorData, EditorStore} from '../../editorStore';
import {EditorStoreContext} from '../../editorStoreContext';

type Props = {
  initialData: EditorData;
  children: ReactNode;
  persistence?: {name: string; storage: StorageAdapter};
};

export function EditorStoreProvider({initialData, children, persistence}: Props) {
  const store = prepareStoreForHydration(
    useLocalStore(() => new EditorStore(initialData)),
  );
  const name = persistence?.name;
  const storage = persistence?.storage;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (name === undefined || storage === undefined) return;
    const handle = persist(store, {
      name,
      storage,
      properties: ['title', 'body'],
      skipHydration: true,
    });
    void handle.rehydrate().catch((error) => console.error('Could not restore persisted state', error));
    return () => handle.dispose();
  }, [store, name, storage]);

  return (
    <EditorStoreContext.Provider value={store}>
      {children}
    </EditorStoreContext.Provider>
  );
}
```

Keep constructors and initializers pure: Strict Mode can evaluate them more than once. Start subscriptions, timers, and storage work in effects with cleanup. The persistence effect depends on the storage adapter and name, so passing a new options object with those same values does not restart it. Keep a custom storage adapter's identity stable too.

The context holds the stable store proxy. Consumers read snapshots through the existing React hook and send edits through store methods:

```tsx
// components/editorTitle/EditorTitle.tsx
import {useClassyStore} from '@codebelt/classy-store/react';
import {useEditorStore} from '../../hooks/useEditorStore';

export function EditorTitle() {
  const store = useEditorStore();
  const title = useClassyStore(store, (state) => state.title);
  return <input value={title} onChange={(event) => store.setTitle(event.target.value)} />;
}
```

Auto-tracking also works: `const state = useClassyStore(useEditorStore())`. Reading fields directly from the mutable store during render does not subscribe to mutations. Avoid creating a module-level bound hook for one store if consumers must select different instances through context.

## Preserve drafts and reset intentionally

`initialData` is an initializer. New props or an ordinary parent render leave the existing store and draft intact. Use a [changed React key](https://react.dev/learn/preserving-and-resetting-state#resetting-state-with-a-key) to create a fresh session:

```tsx
<EditorStoreProvider
  key={`${documentId}:${revision}`}
  initialData={documentData}
>
  <EditorTitle />
</EditorStoreProvider>
```

Change `documentId` when moving to a different document; increment `revision` for an explicit reset. A key change remounts the provider's whole subtree, including nested providers. Resetting a nested provider leaves its parent and siblings intact.

| Event | Store and effect behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Parent render or changed `initialData`, same key | Preserve the existing store and edits |
| Provider key changes | Create a new store and clean up the old subtree |
| Nested provider | Consumers inside it use its independent store |
| Storage name or adapter changes | Keep the store; detach old persistence and load from the new configuration |
| Persistence removed | Keep current state and stop persistence |
| Provider unmounts | React releases its store reference and effect cleanup detaches persistence |

A reset does **not** clear saved data. If the new provider uses the same persistence key, it restores that saved draft. To reset saved data as well, first unmount or disable the old persistence owner, await `storage.removeItem(name)`, then remount. Use distinct storage keys for independent documents or users. Different React providers using the same storage key still share that storage namespace.

Cleanup prevents pending storage reads from applying after disposal, including the discarded first effect in Strict Mode. Such reads still finish and their promises settle; the adapter's I/O is not cancelled. Already-issued writes cannot be undone by cleanup. External code retaining a store can still mutate it after unmount, but its disposed persistence owner and unmounted consumers no longer react. `useLocalStore` does not automatically call application-specific `dispose()` methods.

## Server rendering and hydration

Render a fresh provider for each server request. Transfer only its initial data through the framework's serialization facility, then initialize the client provider from that same data. The provider prepares the initial snapshot before any persistence effect, so a delayed Suspense boundary can hydrate correctly even after another part of the tree restores browser storage. See the [SSR guide](./REACT_SSR.md) for transport and streaming details.

Browser storage belongs in the client setup; do not access `localStorage` at module initialization on the server. Effects do not run during server rendering. The server and client's initial markup must match regardless of whether browser persistence is enabled.

## Regression coverage

`bun run test:react:compatibility` copies the actual example provider, context, hook, and class into isolated installed-package consumers on React 18.0, 18.3, and 19.3. Tests cover sibling and nested isolation, missing providers, stable initialization, keyed resets, Strict Mode, persistence replacement/removal, pending-read cleanup, request isolation, and delayed Suspense hydration with DOM reuse. Strict type checks verify mutable commands, readonly snapshots, selector inference, and provider props.

# Persist Tutorial

`persist()` saves your store's state to storage and restores it on page load. It's a standalone utility function that works with any `createClassyStore()` instance -- no plugins, no middleware, no configuration files. Import it from `@codebelt/classy-store/utils`, call it once, and your store survives page refreshes.

## Getting Started

### 1. Create a store

```ts
import {createClassyStore} from '@codebelt/classy-store';

class TodoStore {
  todos: { text: string; done: boolean }[] = [];
  filter: 'all' | 'active' | 'done' = 'all';

  get remaining() {
    return this.todos.filter((todo) => !todo.done).length;
  }

  addTodo(text: string) {
    this.todos.push({text, done: false});
  }

  toggle(index: number) {
    this.todos[index]!.done = !this.todos[index]!.done;
  }
}

export const todoStore = createClassyStore(new TodoStore());
```

### 2. Persist it

```ts
import {persist} from '@codebelt/classy-store/utils';

const handle = persist(todoStore, {
  name: 'todo-store',
});
```

That's it. On every mutation, `todos` and `filter` are saved to `localStorage`. On next page load, they're restored automatically. The getter `remaining` and the methods are **not** persisted.

### 3. Wait for hydration

```ts
// Async -- await the promise
await handle.hydrated;
console.log('Hydration status:', handle.getSnapshot());

// Sync check
if (handle.isHydrated) {
  // The attempt settled; inspect lastError for a reported failure.
}
```

## Choosing What to Persist

```ts
persist(todoStore, {
  name: 'todo-store',
  properties: ['todos'],  // Only persist todos, not filter
});
```

## Per-Property Transforms

### Dates

```ts
persist(sessionStore, {
  name: 'session',
  properties: [
    'token',
    {
      key: 'expiresAt',
      serialize: (date) => date.toISOString(),
      deserialize: (stored) => new Date(stored as string),
    },
  ],
});
```

### ReactiveMap

```ts
persist(userStore, {
  name: 'user-store',
  properties: [
    {
      key: 'users',
      serialize: (users) => [...users.entries()],
      deserialize: (stored) => reactiveMap(stored as [string, { name: string; role: string }][]),
    },
  ],
});
```

## Debouncing Writes

```ts
persist(formStore, {
  name: 'form-draft',
  debounce: 500,  // Write at most once every 500ms
});
```

## Version Migration

```ts
persist(todoStore, {
  name: 'todo-store',
  version: 2,
  migrate: (state, oldVersion) => {
    if (oldVersion === 0) {
      return {...state, todos: state.items, items: undefined};
    }
    if (oldVersion === 1) {
      return {
        ...state,
        todos: (state.todos as string[]).map((text) => ({text, done: false})),
      };
    }
    return state;
  },
});
```

## Merge Strategies

- **`'shallow'` (default):** Persisted values overwrite store values one key at a time. Properties not in storage keep their class defaults.
- **Custom merge function:** `merge: (persisted, current) => { ... }`

## Cross-Tab Synchronization

```ts
persist(authStore, {
  name: 'auth',
  storage: localStorage,
  syncTabs: true,
});
```

Opt in with `syncTabs: true` for localStorage-backed state. It defaults to false.
Accepted remote updates cancel pending debounced writes without echoing the
restored state back. An event whose value has already been replaced in its
storage area is ignored, so delayed events cannot roll back a newer local save.

## Expiration / TTL

```ts
persist(sessionStore, {
  name: 'session',
  expireIn: 900_000,  // 15 minutes
  clearOnExpire: true,
});

await handle.hydrated;
if (handle.isExpired) {
  router.push('/login');
}
```

## SSR / Next.js Support

```ts
const handle = persist(todoStore, {
  name: 'todo-store',
  skipHydration: true,
});
```

Then hydrate manually in a `useEffect`:

```tsx
function App() {
  useEffect(() => {
    void handle.rehydrate().catch((error) => console.error('Could not restore persisted state', error));
  }, []);

  return <TodoList />;
}
```

## Async Storage (React Native)

```ts
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';

persist(todoStore, {
  name: 'todo-store',
  storage: AsyncStorage,
  syncTabs: false,
});

await handle.hydrated;
```

## Cleanup

```ts
// Clear stored data
await handle.clear();

// Manual save (bypass debounce; rejects on failure)
await handle.save();

// Re-read from storage
await handle.rehydrate();

// Stop persisting; later save/clear/rehydrate calls reject
handle.dispose();
```

## Overlapping async operations

Each handle orders its writes/removals. `save()` captures current state when
requested and waits behind earlier writes; a failed write reports through
`onError` without blocking the queue. `rehydrate()` waits for prior requested
writes/removals, then ignores results superseded by a newer read, save, clear,
accepted storage event, or local edit. Typing during initial async hydration
keeps newer local state. Ignored reads still settle their promises.

`clear()` cancels pending auto-saves and removes stored data after earlier issued
writes finish; later edits can persist again. Cleanup skips queued operations
that have not started, but cannot cancel already-issued adapter I/O. Ordering
is per handle; separate handles sharing an async key need application/adapter
coordination. Async saves are not guaranteed to finish during page unload.

## Quick Reference

| What you want | How to do it |
|---|---|
| Persist everything | `persist(myStore, {name: 'key'})` |
| Persist specific properties | `properties: ['count', 'name']` |
| Handle Dates | `{key: 'date', serialize: (date) => date.toISOString(), deserialize: (stored) => new Date(stored)}` |
| Handle ReactiveMap | `{key: 'map', serialize: (map) => [...map.entries()], deserialize: (stored) => reactiveMap(stored)}` |
| Debounce writes | `debounce: 500` |
| Migrate schema changes | `version: 2, migrate: (state, old) => { ... }` |
| SSR support | `skipHydration: true` + `handle.rehydrate()` in `useEffect` |
| Cross-tab sync | `storage: localStorage, syncTabs: true` |
| Disable cross-tab sync | `syncTabs: false` |
| Use sessionStorage | `storage: sessionStorage` |
| Use AsyncStorage | `storage: AsyncStorage, syncTabs: false` |
| Expire after 15 minutes | `expireIn: 900_000` |
| Auto-clear expired data | `clearOnExpire: true` |
| Check if data expired | `handle.isExpired` |
| Force immediate save | `handle.save()` |
| Clear stored data | `handle.clear()` |
| Stop persisting | `handle.dispose()` |
| Wait for hydration | `await handle.hydrated` |
| Check hydration | `handle.isHydrated` |

SOURCE: https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/docs/DEVTOOLS_TUTORIAL

# DevTools Tutorial

`devtools()` connects a store proxy to the [Redux DevTools](https://github.com/reduxjs/redux-devtools) browser extension for state inspection and time-travel debugging. Every mutation sends a snapshot to the DevTools panel. You can inspect state, jump to any point in history, and the store updates in real-time.

## Getting Started

### 1. Create a store

```ts
import {createClassyStore} from '@codebelt/classy-store';

class CounterStore {
  count = 0;
  step = 1;

  get doubled() {
    return this.count * 2;
  }

  increment() {
    this.count += this.step;
  }

  decrement() {
    this.count -= this.step;
  }

  setStep(step: number) {
    this.step = step;
  }
}

export const counterStore = createClassyStore(new CounterStore());
```

### 2. Connect to DevTools

```ts
import {devtools} from '@codebelt/classy-store/utils';

const disconnect = devtools(counterStore, {name: 'CounterStore'});
```

### 3. Disconnect when done

```ts
disconnect();
```

## Signature

```ts
function devtools<T extends object>(
  proxyStore: T,
  options?: DevtoolsOptions,
): () => void;
```

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `name` | `string` | `'ClassyStore'` | Display name in the DevTools panel |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Set to `false` to disable (returns a noop) |

## Use Cases

### Development-only

```ts
devtools(counterStore, {
  name: 'CounterStore',
  enabled: import.meta.env.DEV,
});
```

### Multiple stores

```ts
devtools(authStore, {name: 'AuthStore'});
devtools(todoStore, {name: 'TodoStore'});
devtools(uiStore, {name: 'UiStore'});
```

### React cleanup

```tsx
function App() {
  useEffect(() => {
    const disconnect = devtools(counterStore, {name: 'CounterStore'});
    return () => disconnect();
  }, []);

  return <Counter />;
}
```

## Quick Reference

| What you want | How to do it |
|---|---|
| Connect a store | `devtools(store, {name: 'MyStore'})` |
| Disconnect | `const dispose = devtools(...); dispose()` |
| Disable in production | `enabled: import.meta.env.DEV` |
| Multiple stores | Call `devtools()` once per store with unique names |
| Use without extension | Works safely — returns a noop if extension is missing |

---
SOURCE: https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/docs/SUBSCRIBE_KEY_TUTORIAL
---

# subscribeKey Tutorial

`subscribeKey()` subscribes to changes on a single property of a store proxy. It's the property-level equivalent of `subscribe()` — instead of firing on every store mutation, it only fires when the specific key you're watching actually changes.

## Getting Started

### 1. Create a store

```ts
import {createClassyStore} from '@codebelt/classy-store';

class SettingsStore {
  theme: 'light' | 'dark' = 'light';
  fontSize = 14;
  language = 'en';

  setTheme(theme: 'light' | 'dark') {
    this.theme = theme;
  }
}

export const settingsStore = createClassyStore(new SettingsStore());
```

### 2. Watch a single key

```ts
import {subscribeKey} from '@codebelt/classy-store/utils';

const unsub = subscribeKey(settingsStore, 'theme', (value, previousValue) => {
  console.log(`Theme changed from "${previousValue}" to "${value}"`);
  document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', value);
});
```

### 3. Unsubscribe when done

```ts
unsub();
```

## Signature

```ts
function subscribeKey<T extends object, K extends keyof T>(
  proxyStore: T,
  key: K,
  callback: (value: Snapshot<T>[K], previousValue: Snapshot<T>[K]) => void,
): () => void;
```

## Use Cases

### Reacting to auth state changes

```ts
subscribeKey(authStore, 'token', (token, previousToken) => {
  if (token && !previousToken) {
    router.push('/dashboard');
  } else if (!token && previousToken) {
    router.push('/login');
  }
});
```

### Syncing with external systems

```ts
subscribeKey(playerStore, 'volume', (volume) => {
  audioContext.gainNode.gain.value = volume;
});

subscribeKey(playerStore, 'track', (track) => {
  document.title = track ? `Playing: ${track}` : 'Music Player';
});
```

## subscribeKey vs subscribe

| | `subscribe()` | `subscribeKey()` |
|---|---|---|
| Fires on | Any mutation in the store | Only when the watched key changes |
| Callback args | `()` (no arguments) | `(value, previousValue)` |
| Use case | General side effects | Property-specific reactions |

## Quick Reference

| What you want | How to do it |
|---|---|
| Watch a single property | `subscribeKey(store, 'key', (val, prev) => { ... })` |
| Stop watching | `const unsub = subscribeKey(...); unsub()` |
| Watch multiple properties | Call `subscribeKey()` once per key |
| Get both old and new value | Callback receives `(value, previousValue)` |

---
SOURCE: https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/docs/HISTORY_TUTORIAL
---

# withHistory Tutorial

`withHistory()` adds undo/redo capability to any store proxy. It maintains a stack of snapshots captured on each mutation. Call `undo()` to go back, `redo()` to go forward, and `pause()`/`resume()` to batch operations that shouldn't create individual history entries.

## Getting Started

### 1. Create a store

```ts
import {createClassyStore} from '@codebelt/classy-store';

class DrawingStore {
  color = '#000000';
  strokeWidth = 2;
  points: { x: number; y: number }[] = [];

  addPoint(x: number, y: number) {
    this.points = [...this.points, { x, y }];
  }

  setColor(color: string) {
    this.color = color;
  }

  setStrokeWidth(width: number) {
    this.strokeWidth = width;
  }

  clear() {
    this.points = [];
  }
}

export const drawingStore = createClassyStore(new DrawingStore());
```

### 2. Attach history

```ts
import {withHistory} from '@codebelt/classy-store/utils';

const history = withHistory(drawingStore);
```

### 3. Undo and redo

```ts
drawingStore.setColor('#ff0000');
drawingStore.setStrokeWidth(5);

history.undo(); // strokeWidth back to 2
history.undo(); // color back to '#000000'
history.redo(); // color is '#ff0000' again
```

### 4. Check availability

```ts
history.canUndo; // true if there's a previous state
history.canRedo; // true if there's a next state
```

```tsx
function UndoRedoButtons() {
  const {canUndo, canRedo} = useHistoryStatus(history);

  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={history.undo} disabled={!canUndo}>Undo</button>
      <button onClick={history.redo} disabled={!canRedo}>Redo</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Signature

```ts
function withHistory<T extends object>(
  proxyStore: T,
  options?: { limit?: number },
): HistoryHandle;
```

### HistoryHandle

| Property/Method | Type | Description |
|-----------------|------|-------------|
| `undo()` | `() => void` | Restore the previous state |
| `redo()` | `() => void` | Restore the next state (after an undo) |
| `canUndo` | `readonly boolean` | Whether there is a previous state |
| `canRedo` | `readonly boolean` | Whether there is a next state |
| `pause()` | `() => void` | Stop recording history entries |
| `resume()` | `() => void` | Resume recording history entries |
| `dispose()` | `() => void` | Unsubscribe and clean up |

## Use Cases

### Text editor with undo

```ts
const editorStore = createClassyStore(new EditorStore());
const history = withHistory(editorStore, { limit: 200 });

document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === 'z') {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (e.shiftKey) {
      history.redo();
    } else {
      history.undo();
    }
  }
});
```

### Batched edits and pause/resume

Synchronous edits in one turn already share a history entry. `pause()` skips notifications delivered while paused; `resume()` enables recording without creating an entry or grouping asynchronous edits into a transaction.

```ts
function pasteBlock(data: Record<string, string>) {
  for (const [id, value] of Object.entries(data)) {
    spreadsheetStore.setCell(id, value);
  }
}
```

## Combining with Other Utilities

### withHistory + persist

```ts
persist(todoStore, { name: 'todos' });
const history = withHistory(todoStore);
// History is in-memory only — doesn't persist across page loads.
```

### withHistory + devtools

```ts
devtools(store, { name: 'MyStore' });
const history = withHistory(store);
// DevTools shows every mutation including undo/redo restores.
```

## Quick Reference

| What you want | How to do it |
|---|---|
| Add undo/redo | `const h = withHistory(store)` |
| Undo | `h.undo()` |
| Redo | `h.redo()` |
| Check if undoable | `h.canUndo` |
| Check if redoable | `h.canRedo` |
| Limit history size | `withHistory(store, { limit: 50 })` |
| Batch as single step | `h.pause(); /* mutations */; h.resume()` |
| Stop tracking | `h.dispose()` |
| Undo all | `while (h.canUndo) h.undo()` |

---
SOURCE: https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/docs/ARCHITECTURE
---

# Classy Store — Architecture

Internal design documentation for contributors and maintainers.

## Three-Layer Architecture

The library is organized into three distinct layers, each with a single responsibility:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph userCode ["User Code"]
    ClassDef["class MyStore { fields, methods, getters }"]
  end

  subgraph layer1 ["Layer 1: Write Proxy (core.ts)"]
    storeFn["createClassyStore(instance)"]
    SetTrap["SET trap: forward write → bump version → notify subscribers"]
    GetTrap["GET trap: return value, bind methods, lazy-wrap nested objects, memoize getters"]
    DeleteTrap["DELETE trap: same as SET"]
    Batch["queueMicrotask: coalesce synchronous mutations → 1 notification"]
    SyncNotify["sync listeners: notify immediately per mutation"]
    DeepProxy["Lazy deep proxy: nested objects/arrays wrapped on first access"]
  end

  subgraph layer2 ["Layer 2: Snapshot (snapshot.ts)"]
    SnapshotFn["snapshot(proxy): immutable deep copy"]
    StructuralShare["Structural sharing: unchanged refs reused across snapshots"]
    Freeze["Object.freeze: enforces immutability"]
    VersionCache["Version-stamped cache: skip rebuild if version unchanged"]
    GetterEval["Getters: memoized per-snapshot + cross-snapshot caching"]
  end

  subgraph layer3 ["Layer 3: React Hook (useClassyStore.ts)"]
    UseStore["useClassyStore(store, selector?)"]
    UseLocalStore["useLocalStore(factory)"]
    USES["useSyncExternalStore"]
    ProxyCompare["proxy-compare: track which snapshot props selector reads"]
    IsChanged["isChanged(prev, next, affected): fine-grained diff"]
    SelectorMode["Selector mode: Object.is or custom isEqual"]
  end

  subgraph component ["React Component"]
    Render["Re-render ONLY when accessed snapshot props change"]
  end

  ClassDef --> storeFn
  storeFn --> SetTrap
  storeFn --> GetTrap
  storeFn --> DeleteTrap
  SetTrap --> SyncNotify
  SetTrap --> Batch
  Batch --> SnapshotFn
  GetTrap --> DeepProxy
  SnapshotFn --> StructuralShare
  StructuralShare --> Freeze
  Freeze --> VersionCache
  VersionCache --> GetterEval
  UseStore --> USES
  USES --> VersionCache
  VersionCache --> ProxyCompare
  ProxyCompare --> IsChanged
  IsChanged --> Render
  SelectorMode --> Render
```

## File Map

The library lives in `packages/classy-store`. Public entry points expose the API;
implementation files and types live with the feature that owns them.

```text
packages/classy-store/
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts                         # Core public entry; no React dependency
│   ├── types.ts                         # Public Snapshot<T> and SubscribeOptions
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── core.ts                      # Write proxies, subscriptions, computed getters
│   │   ├── core.types.ts                # Internal dependency and store bookkeeping types
│   │   ├── core.computed.test.ts        # Write-proxy getter memoization
│   │   └── core.ownership.test.ts       # Child ownership and subscription cleanup
│   ├── snapshot/
│   │   ├── snapshot.ts                  # Immutable snapshots and structural sharing
│   │   └── snapshot.computed.test.ts    # Snapshot getter memoization
│   ├── collections/
│   │   ├── index.ts                     # Public collections entry
│   │   └── collections.ts               # ReactiveMap and ReactiveSet
│   ├── frameworks/
│   │   └── react/
│   │       ├── react.ts                 # Public client entry; exports hooks and factory
│   │       ├── server.ts                # Server-safe prepareStoreForHydration entry
│   │       ├── hooks/
│   │       │   ├── useClassyStore/      # Selector and auto-tracked subscriptions; hook types
│   │       │   ├── useLocalStore/       # Component-scoped store creation
│   │       │   ├── useHistoryStatus/    # Public history status hook
│   │       │   ├── usePersistStatus/    # Public persistence status hook
│   │       │   └── useUtilityStatus/    # Internal shared status subscription hook
│   │       ├── utils/
│   │       │   ├── createStoreHook/     # Bound store hook factory
│   │       │   ├── hydrationSnapshots/  # Shared captured snapshots, held by weak keys
│   │       │   ├── snapshotTargetCache/ # Shared tracking targets
│   │       │   └── trackingReadMap/     # Render-local and committed dependency reads
│   │       ├── testHelpers/            # React fixtures
│   │       └── react.*.test.tsx         # Integration tests grouped by behavior
│   └── utils/
│       ├── index.ts                     # Public utility functions and types
│       ├── persist/
│       │   ├── persist.ts               # Storage queue, hydration, transforms, tab sync
│       │   ├── persist.types.ts         # Public persistence options, status, and handle
│       │   └── persist.*.test.ts        # API, concurrency, and error regressions
│       ├── history/                     # Undo/redo and status
│       ├── devtools/                    # Redux DevTools integration
│       ├── subscribe-key/               # Single-property subscriptions
│       ├── equality/                    # shallowEqual
│       ├── utilityStatus/               # Internal framework-neutral status source
│       ├── cloneSnapshot/               # Internal snapshot cloning
│       └── internal/                    # Proxy and property helpers
├── tests/
│   ├── browser/                         # Real input, hydration, and persistence tests
│   ├── compatibility/                   # Packed-library React version matrix
│   ├── compiler/                        # Compiled consumer fixtures and regressions
│   ├── scoping/                         # Provider isolation, lifecycle, and SSR
│   ├── next/                            # Packed Next.js boundaries and navigation
│   ├── memory/                          # Heap snapshots and retention checks
│   └── performance/                     # Form and list benchmarks
├── tsdown.config.ts                     # Published entry points and bundle settings
└── bunfig.toml                          # happy-dom setup for source tests
```

Tests for core behavior stay beside their implementation. React integration tests
exercise the public client entry, including computed getter behavior. Consumer
fixtures under `tests/` verify the packed library and framework build boundaries.
The other framework adapters remain under `src/frameworks/`.

Runnable examples live in `examples/react` and `examples/nextjs` at the repository
root. This guide and the utility architecture guides live in `website/docs`.

## Layer 1: Write Proxy (`core.ts`)

### Overview

The `createClassyStore()` function wraps a class instance in an ES6 Proxy. All mutations — property writes, array operations, nested object changes — are intercepted. Subscribers are batched by default into a single notification per microtask, while React always uses the synchronous path. Other code can opt into that path when it must observe each mutation immediately.

### Data Flow: Mutation → Notification

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant User as User Code
  participant Proxy as Write Proxy
  participant Target as Raw Target
  participant Internal as StoreInternal
  participant Sync as Sync Subscribers
  participant Micro as queueMicrotask
  participant Batched as Batched Subscribers

  User->>Proxy: store.count = 5
  Proxy->>Target: Reflect.set(target, 'count', 5)
  Proxy->>Internal: bumpVersion(internal) up to root
  Proxy->>Internal: snapshotCache = null (invalidate)
  Proxy->>Sync: notify sync listeners immediately
  Proxy->>Micro: schedule batched notify (if not already scheduled)
  Note over Micro: Coalesces all sync mutations
  User->>Proxy: store.name = 'new'
  Proxy->>Target: Reflect.set(target, 'name', 'new')
  Proxy->>Internal: bumpVersion (version increments again)
  Proxy->>Sync: notify sync listeners again
  Note over Micro: Still same microtask batch
  Micro->>Batched: notify batched listeners once
```

### Internal State Storage

All internal bookkeeping is stored in a `WeakMap<proxy, StoreInternal>`:

```typescript
type StoreInternal = {
  target: object;                           // Raw class instance
  version: number;                          // Monotonically increasing
  batchedListeners: Set<() => void>;        // Subscribers notified once per microtask
  syncListeners: Set<() => void>;           // Subscribers notified immediately per mutation
  childProxies: Map<string|symbol, object>; // Cached child proxies
  childInternals: Map<string|symbol, StoreInternal>;
  parent: StoreInternal | null;             // For version propagation
  notifyScheduled: boolean;                 // Batch dedup flag
  computedCache: Map<string|symbol, ComputedEntry>; // Memoized getter cache
};
```

### Proxy Traps

**SET trap:**
1. Compare old and new values with `Object.is` — noop if equal
2. Clean up child proxy if the property is being replaced
3. Forward write to raw target via `Reflect.set`
4. Bump version for this node and all ancestors
5. Notify sync listeners immediately, then schedule batched listeners via `queueMicrotask` (deduped)

**GET trap (priority order):**
1. **Memoized getter detection** — walk prototype chain with `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`. If a getter is found, call `evaluateComputed()` which checks dependency validity and returns the cached result or re-evaluates with dependency tracking.
2. **Method binding** — if value is a function, bind to proxy so `this.count++` in methods goes through the SET trap. Bound methods are cached.
3. **Nested objects/arrays** — if value passes `canProxy()` (plain object or array), lazily wrap in a child proxy. Child proxies are cached in `childProxies` Map. Also records a dependency if a getter is currently being tracked.
4. **Primitives** — return as-is. Also records a dependency if a getter is currently being tracked.

**DELETE trap:** Same pattern as SET — clean up child proxy, delete from target, bump version, notify sync listeners, and schedule batched listeners.

### Batching via `queueMicrotask`

Array operations like `push()` trigger multiple SET traps (element + length). For ordinary listeners, a dirty flag + `queueMicrotask` coalesces these mutations into one notification:

```
store.items.push('a')
  → SET trap for index 0 → scheduleNotify (flags, queues microtask)
  → SET trap for length  → scheduleNotify (already flagged, skips)
  → microtask fires → notifies listeners ONCE
```

Subscribers opt into immediate timing with `{sync: true}`. Sync subscribers run after version propagation and before the batched microtask. They are intentionally not deduped: two writes mean two sync notifications. Every React hook uses this timing so `useSyncExternalStore` observes the new value during the input event, preserving controlled-input caret position. Selectors can run after each write; React batches rendering within event handlers.

### Version Propagation

When a nested property mutates, versions bump from the mutated node up to the root:

```mermaid
graph TD
  Root["Root (v=10 → v=13)"] --> User["user (v=11 → v=12)"]
  Root --> Settings["settings (v=5, unchanged)"]
  User --> Name["name = 'Bob' (mutation here, v=12)"]
  User --> Age["age = 30 (unchanged)"]
```

This enables structural sharing: when the snapshot layer sees that `settings` has the same version, it returns the cached snapshot reference.

## Layer 2: Immutable Snapshots (`snapshot.ts`)

### Overview

`snapshot(proxy)` creates a deeply frozen, plain-JS copy of the store state. Unchanged sub-trees reuse previous snapshot references (structural sharing).

### Snapshot Creation Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Start["snapshot(proxy)"] --> CheckCache{"Version match\nin snapshotCache?"}
  CheckCache -->|Yes| ReturnCached["Return cached snapshot (O(1))"]
  CheckCache -->|No| CreateSnap["Create new snapshot object"]
  CreateSnap --> IterateKeys["For each own key"]
  IterateKeys --> CheckChild{"Has child\ninternal?"}
  CheckChild -->|Yes| Recurse["Recurse: createSnapshotRecursive(child)"]
  CheckChild -->|No| CheckProxy{"Value is\nplain obj/array?"}
  CheckProxy -->|Yes| DeepClone["deepFreezeClone (cached by identity)"]
  CheckProxy -->|No| CopyValue["Copy as-is (primitive/function)"]
  Recurse --> AssignProp["Assign to snapshot"]
  DeepClone --> AssignProp
  CopyValue --> AssignProp
  AssignProp --> IterateKeys
  IterateKeys -->|Done| Freeze["Object.freeze(snapshot)"]
  Freeze --> Cache["Cache: snapshotCache.set(target, [version, snap])"]
  Cache --> Return["Return frozen snapshot"]
```

### Two Cache Strategies

1. **Tracked sub-trees** (`snapshotCache` — `WeakMap<rawTarget, [version, frozenSnap]>`):
   Objects that have been accessed through the proxy have a `StoreInternal` with version tracking. The snapshot recurses into them and uses version-stamped caching for structural sharing.

2. **Untracked sub-trees** (`untrackedCache` — `WeakMap<rawObject, frozenClone>`):
   Objects never accessed through the proxy are deep-cloned and frozen. The clone is cached by the raw object's identity. Since untracked objects can't be mutated through the proxy, the cache is always fresh.

### Structural Sharing Example

```
Snapshot v1:                    Snapshot v2 (after user.name = 'Bob'):
┌──────────┐                    ┌──────────┐
│ root     │                    │ root     │ (new object)
│ user ────┼──→ {name:'Alice'}  │ user ────┼──→ {name:'Bob'} (new)
│ settings─┼──→ {theme:'dark'}  │ settings─┼──→ {theme:'dark'} (SAME ref ===)
└──────────┘                    └──────────┘
```

`snap2.settings === snap1.settings` because the `settings` sub-tree's version didn't change → cache hit → same reference.

### Getter Evaluation (Memoized)

Snapshots preserve the prototype chain and install lazy-memoizing getters on each snapshot object. Getter results are cached at two levels:

1. **Per-snapshot cache** — repeated access to the same getter on the same snapshot returns the identical reference.
2. **Cross-snapshot cache** — if the properties the getter reads are structurally the same across snapshots (via reference equality from structural sharing), the previous result is returned.

```typescript
class Store {
  count = 5;
  get doubled() { return this.count * 2; }
}

const snap = snapshot(createClassyStore(new Store()));
snap.doubled; // 10 — computed once, cached
snap.doubled; // 10 — same reference (per-snapshot cache hit)
```

## Computed Getter Memoization

Class getters are automatically memoized at two layers — the write proxy and the snapshot — without any user-facing API changes. This is analogous to MobX's `@computed`, but implemented transparently via Proxy.

### Write Proxy Memoization (`core.ts`)

When a getter is accessed on the write proxy, `evaluateComputed()` runs the getter with dependency tracking. A module-level tracker stack records which properties the getter reads on `this`:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  GetterAccess["store.filtered accessed"]
  CheckDeps{"Dependencies\nchanged?"}
  ReturnCached["Return cached value"]
  Recompute["Re-run getter with\ndependency tracking"]
  CacheResult["Cache result + deps"]

  GetterAccess --> CheckDeps
  CheckDeps -->|No| ReturnCached
  CheckDeps -->|Yes| Recompute
  Recompute --> CacheResult
  CacheResult --> ReturnCached
```

**Dependency types:**
- **Sub-tree dep** (`kind: 'version'`): the getter read a nested object/array. Validated by comparing `internal.version` — O(1) per dep.
- **Primitive dep** (`kind: 'value'`): the getter read a primitive. Validated by `Object.is(target[prop], recordedValue)` — O(1) per dep.

**Nested getter support:** when getter A reads getter B, B pushes its own frame onto the tracker stack. If B returns cached, A's deps include B's deps (propagated). If B recomputes, the underlying reads naturally propagate to A's tracker.

### Snapshot Memoization (`snapshot.ts`)

Since snapshots are frozen, a getter's result can never change for a given snapshot. But more importantly, getter results are stable **across** snapshots when dependencies haven't changed:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SnapGetter["snap.filtered accessed"]
  PerSnapCheck{"Per-snapshot\ncache hit?"}
  PerSnapReturn["Return cached ref"]
  CrossSnapCheck{"Cross-snapshot\ndeps unchanged?"}
  CrossSnapReturn["Return prev result"]
  Compute["Run getter with dep tracking,\nrecord which this.X were read"]
  CacheBoth["Cache in per-snapshot + cross-snapshot"]

  SnapGetter --> PerSnapCheck
  PerSnapCheck -->|Yes| PerSnapReturn
  PerSnapCheck -->|No| CrossSnapCheck
  CrossSnapCheck -->|Yes| CrossSnapReturn
  CrossSnapCheck -->|No| Compute
  Compute --> CacheBoth
```

**Cross-snapshot mechanism:**
1. First evaluation: a lightweight tracking Proxy records which `this` properties the getter reads and their values.
2. On subsequent snapshots: for each recorded property, check `Object.is(currentSnap[prop], previousValue)`.
3. Structural sharing guarantees that unchanged sub-trees have the same reference — so if `this.todos` hasn't changed, the reference comparison passes and the cached result is returned.
4. For getters reading other getters (e.g., `get filteredCount() { return this.filtered.length; }`): the inner getter is itself memoized, so it returns a stable reference, which the outer getter's dep check recognizes as unchanged.

**Impact on `useClassyStore`:** The existing hook benefits automatically — no changes needed:
- **Selector mode:** `useClassyStore(store, (state) => state.filtered)` gets a stable reference from the memoized snapshot getter. `Object.is` correctly detects "no change" without `shallowEqual`.
- **Auto-tracked mode:** `proxy-compare`'s `isChanged` gets stable references from snapshot getters, reducing false positives.

## Layer 3: React Hook (`hooks/useClassyStore/useClassyStore.ts`)

### Overview

`useClassyStore` uses `useSyncExternalStore` for tear-free React integration. React subscriptions always notify synchronously, allowing controlled inputs to observe updates during their event. The React API has no timing option; ordinary core subscriptions remain batched. It supports two modes:

### Server rendering and hydration

`prepareStoreForHydration(store)` captures an immutable snapshot in a WeakMap keyed by the exact store proxy. It returns the same mutable proxy and preserves the first capture on repeated calls. Capturing is explicit at bootstrap, before rendering or persistence, because a delayed Suspense boundary may not call its hook until after the live store changes.

Prepared stores supply that snapshot through `getServerSnapshot`; ordinary `getSnapshot` still reads live state. Each selector has separate server and live caches. When React reads the hydration result, it can seed the live cache with that result so unchanged inputs and equal selections retain their references without overwriting committed selections during rendering. Client-only mounts never evaluate the server selector.

The capture stays available for the store's lifetime, including later boundaries or roots. It is never cleared when the first consumer mounts. Unprepared stores keep the existing current-snapshot behavior. Core mutation timing, ordinary subscriptions, and `snapshot(store)` are unchanged.

### Mode 1: Selector

```typescript
const count = useClassyStore(myStore, (state) => state.count);
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant React as React (useSyncExternalStore)
  participant Hook as useClassyStore
  participant Snap as snapshot()
  participant Selector as selector(snap)

  React->>Hook: getSnapshot()
  Hook->>Snap: snapshot(proxy)
  Snap-->>Hook: frozen snapshot
  Hook->>Hook: Same snapshot ref? → return cached result
  Hook->>Selector: selector(snapshot)
  Selector-->>Hook: selected value
  Hook->>Hook: Object.is(prev, next)?
  alt Same value
    Hook-->>React: return cached (no re-render)
  else Different value
    Hook-->>React: return new value (re-render)
  end
```

**Equality chain:**
1. Same store, selector, equality function, and snapshot reference? → reuse the cached result (O(1))
2. Run selector → compare result with `Object.is` (or `options.isEqual`)
3. Same result → return previous reference (no re-render)

**Controlled input timing:**

```typescript
const name = useClassyStore(formStore, (state) => state.name);
```

The hook always calls the core `subscribe()` with `{sync: true}`. Ordinary listeners still batch with `queueMicrotask`. This timing is independent of React's own render scheduling and does not provide atomic transactions across several writes.

### Mode 2: Auto-tracked (selectorless)

```typescript
const snap = useClassyStore(myStore);
// snap.count — tracked
// snap.user.name — tracked
```

Each render creates its own `affected` map and raw-snapshot getter; the hook retains a proxy cache across renders. `useSyncExternalStore` receives a cached raw snapshot: unchanged tracked values return the previous snapshot for that render. After reading it, the hook wraps the snapshot with `createProxy` to record the component's property reads.

A parent re-render starts from current store data and a render-local `TrackingReadMap`. It lazily copies committed operation records for reused immutable snapshot objects, including structurally shared children. This retains reads skipped by React Compiler or manual memoization. Sets are copied before recording new reads, so suspended and abandoned renders cannot change committed dependencies. An effect publishes only committed reads into a WeakMap; old snapshot objects can be collected without retaining a chain of prior render maps.

The adapter follows the operation-record/Set layout of the pinned `proxy-compare` 3 dependency without hardcoding its private field names. Compiled regressions cover value reads, `in`, `Object.hasOwn`, and key enumeration. Reused snapshot objects conservatively retain prior committed dependencies, so changing a conditional branch may cause an extra render before that object's identity changes. Explicit selectors provide selected-value equality when stricter filtering is needed.

Snapshot creation marks only library-created snapshot nodes with `markToTrack`, including class and null-prototype objects. This enables field tracking without altering opaque leaves such as native maps and dates. Nodes containing object-valued symbol fields use whole-node comparison to avoid a frozen-symbol limitation in `proxy-compare` 3; updates remain reactive with coarser render filtering.

**How `proxy-compare` works:**
- `createProxy(snapshot, affected)` records properties read into the render's map; committed records are retained separately with weak snapshot keys.
- `isChanged(previousSnapshot, nextSnapshot, affected)` checks whether a tracked property differs.
- Unchanged tracked properties suppress subscription-driven renders; `snapshot()` retains its existing identity cache and structural sharing.

## Dependency Graph

```mermaid
graph LR
  reactEntry["/react client entry"] --> hook["useClassyStore.ts"]
  reactEntry --> localHook["useLocalStore.ts"]
  reactEntry --> factory["createStoreHook.ts"]
  factory --> hook
  factory --> core["core.ts"]
  localHook --> core
  hook --> core
  hook --> snapshot["snapshot.ts"]
  hook --> proxyCompare["proxy-compare"]
  hook --> hydration["hydrationSnapshots.ts"]
  serverEntry["/react/server entry"] --> hydration
  serverEntry --> snapshot
  serverEntry --> core
  snapshot --> core
  snapshot --> types["types.ts: public types"]
  snapshot --> coreTypes["core.types.ts: internal types"]
  snapshot --> internal["utils/internal/internal.ts"]
  core --> types
  core --> coreTypes
  core --> internal
  index["Core entry: index.ts"] --> core
  index --> snapshot
  index --> equality["equality.ts"]
  index --> types

  subgraph utilities ["Utilities (utils/)"]
    persist["persist.ts"]
    devtools["devtools.ts"]
    subscribeKey["subscribe-key.ts"]
    withHistory["history.ts"]
    status["utilityStatus.ts"]
  end

  persist --> core
  persist --> snapshot
  persist --> internal
  persist --> status
  devtools --> core
  devtools --> snapshot
  subscribeKey --> core
  subscribeKey --> snapshot
  withHistory --> core
  withHistory --> snapshot
  withHistory --> status
  reactEntry --> statusHooks["useHistoryStatus / usePersistStatus"]
  statusHooks --> sharedHook["useUtilityStatus.ts"]
```

The client entry owns the React boundary. Core, snapshots, collections, and
utilities remain framework-neutral. React status hooks share an internal hook;
the status source itself lives with the utilities and has no React dependency.
`types.ts` contains public core types, while `core.types.ts` describes private
bookkeeping. Persistence contracts live in `persist.types.ts` and are exported
through the public utilities entry.

## Key Design Decisions

### Why ES6 Proxy instead of `Object.defineProperty`?

ES6 Proxy supports intercepting property creation, deletion, and arbitrary key access — not just known properties. This is essential for arrays (index access) and dynamic objects. All modern browsers and Node.js/Bun support Proxy natively.

### Why `queueMicrotask` for batching?

`queueMicrotask` runs after the current synchronous code but before the next paint/timer. For ordinary subscribers, this means:
- Multiple mutations in the same event handler → 1 notification
- Array `push` (which triggers multiple SET traps) → 1 notification
- No risk of missing updates (unlike `requestAnimationFrame`)

### Why structural sharing in snapshots?

Without structural sharing, `Object.is(prevSelector, nextSelector)` would always return `false` for object/array selectors because each snapshot creates new objects. Structural sharing ensures unchanged sub-trees maintain reference equality, making selectors efficient without custom equality functions.

### Why `proxy-compare` for auto-tracking?

`proxy-compare` (~1KB, maintained by the creator of Valtio/Zustand/Jotai) provides battle-tested property access tracking. It wraps a frozen object in a Proxy that records reads, then efficiently diffs only the accessed properties between snapshots. This eliminates the need for manual selectors in many cases.

### Why `useSyncExternalStore` instead of `useState` + `useEffect`?

`useSyncExternalStore` is React's official API for external stores. It:
- Prevents tearing (concurrent mode safe)
- Integrates with React's scheduler
- Works with server-side rendering (via `getServerSnapshot`)
- Is the same API used by Zustand, Redux, and Valtio

### Why `WeakMap` for internal state?

Storing internals in a `WeakMap<proxy, StoreInternal>` instead of on the proxy itself:
- Doesn't pollute the user's object with library metadata
- Allows garbage collection when the store is no longer referenced
- Prevents conflicts with user-defined properties

### Why subclass inheritance works

No special handling is needed — three mechanisms in the existing design make it work automatically:

1. **Methods** — The GET trap uses `Reflect.get(target, prop)`, which naturally walks the JavaScript prototype chain. Methods from any ancestor class are found and bound to the proxy via `.bind(receiver)`, so `this` mutations inside inherited methods go through the SET trap. **Important:** Arrow function properties (`increment = () => {}`) are own properties whose `this` is lexically bound to the raw instance at construction time. `.bind()` is a no-op on arrow functions, so mutations inside them bypass the proxy entirely. Always use prototype methods (`increment() {}`) for reactive mutations.

2. **Getters** — `findGetterDescriptor()` (in `utils.ts`) walks the prototype chain with `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` and returns the first (most-derived) getter found. For snapshots, `collectGetters()` (in `snapshot.ts`) walks the full chain using a `seen` Set to ensure overridden getters are collected only once — the most-derived version wins.

3. **Snapshot prototype** — `createSnapshotRecursive()` creates snapshot objects with `Object.create(Object.getPrototypeOf(target))`, preserving the full prototype chain. This means `snapshot(store) instanceof DerivedClass` is `true`, and `installMemoizedGetters()` installs getters from all levels with cross-snapshot memoization.

`super.method()` calls also work because they use the language-level prototype dispatch mechanism, which resolves to the parent method with `this` still bound to the proxy.

## Performance Characteristics

| Operation | Complexity | Notes |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Property read | O(1) | Direct Proxy GET trap |
| Property write | O(depth) | Versions bump from node to root |
| Notification | O(listeners) | Ordinary listeners once per microtask; React listeners per mutation |
| Getter (cache hit) | O(deps) | Check deps validity, return cached |
| Getter (cache miss) | O(getter body) | Re-evaluates with dep tracking |
| Snapshot (cache hit) | O(1) | Version check only |
| Snapshot (cache miss) | O(changed branches) | Structural sharing skips unchanged |
| Snapshot getter (same snap) | O(1) | Per-snapshot cache hit |
| Snapshot getter (cross-snap) | O(deps) | Reference comparison via structural sharing |
| Selector equality | O(1) for primitives | `Object.is` check |
| Auto-track diff | O(accessed props) | `proxy-compare` checks only read props |

---
SOURCE: https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/docs/PERSIST_ARCHITECTURE
---

# Persist Utility — Architecture

Internal design documentation for the `persist()` utility in `@codebelt/classy-store/utils`.

## Design Principles

1. **Standalone utility, not middleware.** `persist` uses `subscribe` and `snapshot`, plus an internal version helper for stale-read protection.
2. **Tree-shakeable.** Lives in `@codebelt/classy-store/utils`. Applications that don't use persistence pay zero cost.
3. **Storage-agnostic.** The `StorageAdapter` interface accepts sync (`localStorage`, `sessionStorage`) and async (`AsyncStorage`, `localForage`) implementations.
4. **Class-aware.** Getters and methods are automatically excluded from persistence. Only source-of-truth data properties are saved.

## How It Hooks Into the Existing Architecture

`persist` sits beside the existing three-layer architecture as an independent consumer:

- **Save flow:** `subscribe callback` → `debounce timer` → `snapshot(proxy)` → `pick properties` → `per-property serialize` → `JSON.stringify envelope` → `storage.setItem()`
- **Restore flow:** `storage.getItem()` → `JSON.parse` → `version check + migrate` → `per-property deserialize` → `merge strategy` → `proxy[key] = value` → triggers SET trap → reactivity

## Storage Envelope

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "state": {
    "todos": [{"text": "Buy milk", "done": false}],
    "filter": "all"
  },
  "expiresAt": 1700000000000
}
```

The `version` field is always present (default `0`). The `expiresAt` field is a Unix epoch timestamp (ms) and is only present when `expireIn` is set. It resets on every write.

## Merge Strategies

| Strategy | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `'shallow'` (default) | `{ ...current, ...persisted }` — persisted keys overwrite, new keys keep defaults |
| `'replace'` | Same as shallow at top level |
| Custom `fn` | `fn(persisted, current)` — full control |

## Cross-Tab Sync

`syncTabs` defaults to false. When enabled for localStorage-backed state, the
utility listens for storage events from other same-origin tabs. It ignores
obsolete event values and suppresses echo writes while applying accepted updates.

## PersistHandle API

| Method/Property | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `dispose()` | Cancel debounce/listeners, ignore pending reads, and skip queued operations not yet started. Already-issued adapter I/O is not cancelled. Idempotent. |
| `hydrated` | Resolves when a hydration attempt settles, including failure or a superseded read. |
| `isHydrated` | Readonly boolean indicating a settled hydration attempt. |
| `isExpired` | Readonly boolean; true when hydration found expired data. |
| `save()` | Cancel debounce, capture current state, and enqueue its write. |
| `clear()` | Cancel pending auto-saves and enqueue removal after prior writes. |
| `rehydrate()` | Wait for prior writes, apply only if the read remains current, and await expired-data removal when enabled. |
| `getSnapshot()` / `getServerSnapshot()` | Cached current / initial readonly status. |
| `subscribe(listener)` | Observe status; returns listener cleanup. |

## Property Resolution

On initialization, `resolveProperties()` determines which keys to persist:
- If `properties` is provided: each entry is either a string key or a `PropertyTransform` descriptor.
- If `properties` is omitted: takes a snapshot of the store, iterates `Object.keys()`, and excludes getters (detected via prototype chain) and methods (`typeof value === 'function'`).

---
SOURCE: https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/docs/FRAMEWORK_ADAPTERS
---

# Framework Adapters

`@codebelt/classy-store` provides first-class integrations for Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Angular. Each adapter follows the idiomatic reactive pattern for its framework.

## Installation

Install only the peer dependencies you need:

```bash
# Vue
npm install @codebelt/classy-store vue

# Svelte
npm install @codebelt/classy-store svelte

# Solid
npm install @codebelt/classy-store solid-js

# Angular
npm install @codebelt/classy-store @angular/core
```

## Vue 3

**Import:** `@codebelt/classy-store/vue`

**Function:** `useStore<T>(proxyStore: T): ShallowRef<Snapshot<T>>`

Returns a Vue `ShallowRef` that holds the current immutable snapshot. The ref updates whenever the store mutates. Automatically unsubscribes via `onUnmounted`.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store/vue';
import { todoStore } from './stores';

// state is a ShallowRef<Snapshot<TodoStore>>
const state = useStore(todoStore);
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <p>{{ state.remaining }} items remaining</p>
    <ul>
      <li v-for="(todo, index) in state.filtered" :key="index">
        <input
          type="checkbox"
          :checked="todo.done"
          @change="todoStore.toggle(index)"
        />
        {{ todo.text }}
      </li>
    </ul>
    <button @click="todoStore.addTodo('New task')">Add</button>
  </div>
</template>
```

**How it works internally:**

```ts
import { onUnmounted, shallowRef } from 'vue';
import { subscribe } from '@codebelt/classy-store';
import { snapshot } from '@codebelt/classy-store';

export function useStore<T extends object>(proxyStore: T): ShallowRef<Snapshot<T>> {
  const state = shallowRef(snapshot(proxyStore));

  const unsubscribe = subscribe(proxyStore, () => {
    state.value = snapshot(proxyStore);
  });

  onUnmounted(unsubscribe);

  return state;
}
```

**Key notes:**
- Uses `shallowRef` (not `ref`) because snapshots are already deeply frozen — no deep Vue reactivity is needed.
- The unsubscribe callback is registered with `onUnmounted` — must be called inside a component's `setup()` or `<script setup>`.
- Access snapshot properties directly: `state.value.count` in JS, or `state.count` in template (Vue auto-unwraps top-level refs in templates).
- Actions are called directly on the store proxy: `todoStore.addTodo('text')`.

**With a store class:**

```ts
// stores.ts
import { createClassyStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store';

class CounterStore {
  count = 0;
  get doubled() { return this.count * 2; }
  increment() { this.count++; }
}

export const counterStore = createClassyStore(new CounterStore());
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store/vue';
import { counterStore } from './stores';

const state = useStore(counterStore);
// state.value.count, state.value.doubled — both reactive
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="counterStore.increment()">
    Count: {{ state.count }} (doubled: {{ state.doubled }})
  </button>
</template>
```

---

## Svelte 4 / 5

**Import:** `@codebelt/classy-store/svelte`

**Function:** `toSvelteStore<T>(proxyStore: T): ClassyReadable<Snapshot<T>>`

Returns a Svelte-compatible readable store (implements the `{ subscribe }` contract). Use with Svelte's `$store` auto-subscription syntax or call `.subscribe()` manually.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { toSvelteStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store/svelte';
  import { todoStore } from './stores';

  // Convert to a Svelte-compatible readable store
  const store = toSvelteStore(todoStore);
  // Use $store for auto-subscription (Svelte compiler handles cleanup)
</script>

<p>{$store.remaining} items remaining</p>

<ul>
  {#each $store.filtered as todo, index}
    <li>
      <input
        type="checkbox"
        checked={todo.done}
        on:change={() => todoStore.toggle(index)}
      />
      {todo.text}
    </li>
  {/each}
</ul>

<button on:click={() => todoStore.addTodo('New task')}>Add</button>
```

**How it works internally:**

```ts
export interface ClassyReadable<T> {
  subscribe(run: (value: T) => void): () => void;
}

export function toSvelteStore<T extends object>(
  proxyStore: T,
): ClassyReadable<Snapshot<T>> {
  return {
    subscribe(run: (value: Snapshot<T>) => void): () => void {
      // Svelte contract: call immediately with current value
      run(snapshot(proxyStore));

      return subscribe(proxyStore, () => {
        run(snapshot(proxyStore));
      });
    },
  };
}
```

**Key notes:**
- Follows the Svelte store contract: `subscribe` is called immediately with the current value, then on every change. Returns an unsubscribe function.
- The `$store` syntax auto-subscribes and auto-unsubscribes — no manual cleanup needed in Svelte components.
- `toSvelteStore` can be called at module level (outside a component), unlike the Vue/Solid/Angular adapters which must be called during component initialization.
- The `ClassyReadable<T>` interface matches Svelte's built-in `Readable<T>` contract for full compatibility.
- Actions are called directly on the original store proxy: `todoStore.addTodo('text')` — not on the converted store.

**Typed usage:**

```ts
// Convert once at module level
import { toSvelteStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store/svelte';
import { todoStore } from './stores';

export const $todos = toSvelteStore(todoStore);
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { $todos } from './svelte-stores';
  // $todos.remaining, $todos.filtered — all typed as Snapshot<TodoStore>
</script>
```

---

## Solid.js

**Import:** `@codebelt/classy-store/solid`

**Function:** `useStore<T>(proxyStore: T): () => Snapshot<T>`

Returns a Solid signal getter `() => Snapshot<T>`. Call it in JSX to access the current snapshot. Automatically cleans up via `onCleanup`.

```tsx
import { useStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store/solid';
import { todoStore } from './stores';

function TodoList() {
  // state is a signal getter: () => Snapshot<TodoStore>
  const state = useStore(todoStore);

  return (
    <div>
      <p>{state().remaining} items remaining</p>
      <ul>
        {state().filtered.map((todo, index) => (
          <li>
            <input
              type="checkbox"
              checked={todo.done}
              onChange={() => todoStore.toggle(index)}
            />
            {todo.text}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <button onClick={() => todoStore.addTodo('New task')}>Add</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

**How it works internally:**

```ts
import { createSignal, onCleanup } from 'solid-js';
import { subscribe } from '@codebelt/classy-store';
import { snapshot } from '@codebelt/classy-store';

export function useStore<T extends object>(proxyStore: T): () => Snapshot<T> {
  const [state, setState] = createSignal<Snapshot<T>>(snapshot(proxyStore));

  const unsubscribe = subscribe(proxyStore, () => {
    setState(() => snapshot(proxyStore));
  });

  onCleanup(unsubscribe);

  return state;
}
```

**Key notes:**
- Returns a signal getter (a function). You must call it — `state()` — to access the snapshot value. This is idiomatic Solid.js.
- The update uses the functional form `setState(() => snapshot(proxyStore))` to avoid Solid treating the snapshot as a setter function.
- Must be called inside a Solid component or reactive root (like `createRoot`), since it uses `onCleanup`.
- `onCleanup` is called when the reactive owner is disposed — typically when the component unmounts.
- Fine-grained reactivity: Solid tracks which signal properties are accessed. Accessing `state().count` in JSX creates a dependency on that signal.
- Actions are called directly on the store proxy: `todoStore.addTodo('text')`.

---

## Angular

**Import:** `@codebelt/classy-store/angular`

**Function:** `injectStore<T>(proxyStore: T): Signal<Snapshot<T>>`

Returns a readonly Angular `Signal<Snapshot<T>>`. Uses Angular's `inject(DestroyRef)` for automatic cleanup when the component or service is destroyed.

```typescript
// counter.component.ts
import { Component, computed } from '@angular/core';
import { injectStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store/angular';
import { counterStore } from './stores';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-counter',
  standalone: true,
  template: `
    <div>
      <p>Count: {{ state().count }}</p>
      <p>Doubled: {{ doubled() }}</p>
      <button (click)="increment()">Increment</button>
    </div>
  `,
})
export class CounterComponent {
  // state is Signal<Snapshot<CounterStore>>
  readonly state = injectStore(counterStore);

  // Use computed() to derive values from the signal
  readonly doubled = computed(() => this.state().count * 2);

  increment() {
    counterStore.increment();
  }
}
```

**How it works internally:**

```ts
import { DestroyRef, inject, signal, type Signal, type WritableSignal } from '@angular/core';
import { subscribe } from '@codebelt/classy-store';
import { snapshot } from '@codebelt/classy-store';

export function injectStore<T extends object>(proxyStore: T): Signal<Snapshot<T>> {
  const state: WritableSignal<Snapshot<T>> = signal(snapshot(proxyStore));
  const destroyRef = inject(DestroyRef);

  const unsubscribe = subscribe(proxyStore, () => {
    state.set(snapshot(proxyStore));
  });

  destroyRef.onDestroy(unsubscribe);

  return state.asReadonly();
}
```

**Key notes:**
- Must be called in an **injection context** — inside a component constructor, `inject()` call, or an `@Injectable` service constructor. Do not call it outside Angular's DI tree.
- Returns a readonly signal (`Signal<T>`, not `WritableSignal<T>`). Consumers cannot mutate the signal directly.
- Uses `DestroyRef` (available since Angular 16) for automatic cleanup — no need to manually unsubscribe in `ngOnDestroy`.
- Requires Angular 17+ (signals were stable in Angular 17).
- Use Angular's `computed()` to derive values: `readonly total = computed(() => this.state().items.length)`.
- Combine with `effect()` for side effects: `effect(() => console.log(this.state().count))`.
- Actions are called directly on the store proxy: `counterStore.increment()` — not through the signal.

**Usage in a service:**

```typescript
import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { injectStore } from '@codebelt/classy-store/angular';
import { todoStore } from './stores';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class TodoService {
  // Works in services too — inject context is available in constructors
  readonly todos = injectStore(todoStore);

  addTodo(text: string) {
    todoStore.addTodo(text);
  }
}
```

---

## Framework Adapter Summary

| Framework | Import | Function | Return type | Cleanup mechanism |
|-----------|--------|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| Vue 3 | `@codebelt/classy-store/vue` | `useStore(store)` | `ShallowRef<Snapshot<T>>` | `onUnmounted` |
| Svelte 4/5 | `@codebelt/classy-store/svelte` | `toSvelteStore(store)` | `ClassyReadable<Snapshot<T>>` | `$store` syntax / manual unsubscribe |
| Solid.js | `@codebelt/classy-store/solid` | `useStore(store)` | `() => Snapshot<T>` | `onCleanup` |
| Angular | `@codebelt/classy-store/angular` | `injectStore(store)` | `Signal<Snapshot<T>>` | `DestroyRef.onDestroy` |

All adapters:
- Accept any `createClassyStore()` proxy
- Subscribe to batched mutations via `subscribe()`
- Update when `snapshot()` changes
- Clean up their subscription automatically when the component/owner is destroyed
- Return immutable snapshots (deeply frozen objects)
- Require calling actions directly on the store proxy — not on the returned reactive value

---
SOURCE: https://codebelt.github.io/classy-store/docs/REACT_NEXT
---

# Next.js App Router

Pass initial data from a Server Component to a Client Component, then construct
the class store inside the client boundary. That component also renders on the
server for the initial request, so prepare its snapshot before persistence or
other effects start. The browser constructs its own store from the same data.

Do not pass a store proxy or class instance across the React Server Component
boundary. Use a plain data object containing the fields the client needs.
React defines the supported [serializable prop types](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types-returned-by-server-components).

## Package boundaries

| Entry | App Router use |
| --- | --- |
| `@codebelt/classy-store` | Core store creation and snapshots in server or client modules. |
| `@codebelt/classy-store/collections` | Reactive collections in server or client modules. |
| `@codebelt/classy-store/utils` | Server-safe imports; configure browser storage and effects inside Client Components. |
| `@codebelt/classy-store/react` | Client hooks. The published ESM and CommonJS entries carry `use client`. |
| `@codebelt/classy-store/react/server` | `prepareStoreForHydration` without importing React hooks; safe in Server Components and ordinary SSR code. |

Components that use hooks still need their own client boundary. Do not call
`useClassyStore`, `useLocalStore`, or `createStoreHook` in a Server Component.
Preparing a store in an RSC module does not transfer that store or its capture
to the browser; initialize and prepare the browser counterpart separately.
Both preparation exports use the same capture cache within a module graph.

## A route-owned store

Define the class in a regular module that has no browser effects:

```ts
// stores/profile/profile.store.ts
export type ProfileData = {name: string; visits: number};

export class ProfileStore {
  name: string;
  visits: number;

  constructor(initialData: ProfileData) {
    this.name = initialData.name;
    this.visits = initialData.visits;
  }

  recordVisit() {
    this.visits++;
  }
}
```

Construct and prepare it inside the Client Component:

```tsx
// components/profileEditor/ProfileEditor.tsx
'use client';

import {useClassyStore, useLocalStore} from '@codebelt/classy-store/react';
import {prepareStoreForHydration} from '@codebelt/classy-store/react/server';
import {type ProfileData, ProfileStore} from '../../stores/profile/profile.store';

export function ProfileEditor({initialData}: {initialData: ProfileData}) {
  const store = prepareStoreForHydration(
    useLocalStore(() => new ProfileStore(initialData)),
  );
  const state = useClassyStore(store);

  return (
    <div>
      <input
        aria-label="Name"
        value={state.name}
        onChange={(event) => { store.name = event.target.value; }}
      />
      <button type="button" onClick={() => store.recordVisit()}>
        Visits: {state.visits}
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The Server Component supplies data and an intentional reset key:

```tsx
// app/profile/page.tsx
import {ProfileEditor} from '../../components/profileEditor/ProfileEditor';

type Props = {searchParams: Promise<{name?: string}>};

export default async function ProfilePage({searchParams}: Props) {
  const {name = 'Ada'} = await searchParams;
  return <ProfileEditor key={name} initialData={{name, visits: 0}} />;
}
```

The key determines when a mounted editor gets a new store. A new `initialData`
object alone does not reset `useLocalStore` or its prepared snapshot. Avoid
module-level server stores; construct request state inside the request instead.

## Streaming, persistence, and navigation

Attach persistence in an effect after preparation, call `rehydrate()` there,
and call `handle.dispose()` during cleanup. The [SSR guide](./REACT_SSR.md) shows
this pattern. If persistence restores before a streamed boundary hydrates,
the boundary first reads the prepared server data, then catches up to live
state. Keep the initial server and browser payloads identical.

For a store shared across routes, place its Client Provider in the appropriate
layout. Put route-specific providers below that layout and use keys when a
route identity change should reset them. See the [typed context example](./REACT_SCOPING.md).
`router.refresh()` merges new server output; it does not inherently reset a
mounted client store. Choose explicitly whether refreshed data should update
the existing store or replace its provider via a key.

The integration tests use the default App Router configuration with
`cacheComponents: false`. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js can use React
Activity to preserve hidden route state while cleaning up its effects. Returning
to a hidden route can resume the same store; effect cleanup does not necessarily
mean the instance was destroyed. See [Next.js state preservation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state).

## Tested package consumer

Run `bun run test:react:next` from the repository root. It installs the package
tarball into an isolated Next.js 16.4.2 / React 19.3.1 app and runs clean
production Turbopack builds with React Compiler off and on. Tests verify the
actual compiler-generated selector and tracking functions, request isolation,
real inputs, streamed response ordering, delayed hydration without replacing
server DOM, navigation, refresh, and persistence cleanup. They also exercise
the server-safe APIs under React's `react-server` export condition and verify
shared hydration captures across public entry points.

This matrix covers the stated versions and default navigation behavior. It
does not establish compatibility with every Next.js version, bundler, or
Cache Components configuration.

Next App Router can supply its own React runtime. The test evidence records the
actual browser `React.version`; this Next.js version uses
`19.3.0-canary-278794d7-20261002`, while the installed React package is 19.3.1.
